header: AUN-INI-105 -- INI MCQ .pdf, Chapter 11 "Nematoda" (pp.112-130, 164 items). Lane author13, Q111-164. This batch authors the filarial/tissue-nematode vector-and-eponym cluster (article NEMATODA-5): 10 new AUN-INI-105 concepts (one, Simulium/Onchocerca, backs two reversed-framing questions Q146+Q157) plus 1 question (Q161) that reuses lane 10's own cutaneous-larva-migrans concept directly.

questions.title: Brugia malayi's habitat is the lymphatics
questions.question: Lymphatics are the habitat of ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Onchocerca volvulus adults live in subcutaneous fibrous nodules, not in the lymphatics.
explanations.B: Correct. Brugia malayi, like its close relative Wuchereria bancrofti, is a lymphatic-dwelling filarial nematode: its adult worms live coiled within the lymphatics and lymph nodes, where the resulting lymphatic inflammation and obstruction produce lymphoedema and, in chronic cases, elephantiasis of the limbs. This lymphatic habitat is the defining feature that groups Brugia malayi with Wuchereria bancrofti as the two classic causes of lymphatic filariasis. Its microfilariae, released from these lymphatic adults, then circulate periodically in the peripheral blood, from where they are taken up by a mosquito vector.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Strongyloides stercoralis adults live in the mucosa of the small intestine, not in the lymphatics.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Loa loa adults migrate through subcutaneous and connective tissues (giving rise to Calabar swellings and the classic subconjunctival passage of the worm), not through the lymphatics.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the lymphatics as the habitat of adult Brugia malayi, alongside Wuchereria bancrofti.

questions.title: Simulium is the vector of Onchocerca volvulus
questions.question: Simulium is a vector of ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Wuchereria bancrofti is transmitted by culicine (and other) mosquitoes, not by Simulium.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Brugia malayi is transmitted by Mansonia and Anopheles mosquitoes, not by Simulium.
explanations.C: Correct. Simulium, the blackfly, is the arthropod vector of Onchocerca volvulus. Simulium flies breed in the fast-flowing, well-oxygenated water of rivers and streams, and it is this riverine breeding habitat, combined with the blindness Onchocerca volvulus can cause, that gives onchocerciasis its common name, 'river blindness'. During a blood meal taken near the riverbank, an infected Simulium fly deposits infective third-stage larvae onto the skin, which then enter through the bite wound.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Loa loa is transmitted by the Chrysops (mango, deer) fly, not by Simulium.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Simulium (the blackfly) as the vector of Onchocerca volvulus.

questions.title: Cyclops is the intermediate host for Diphyllobothrium and Dracunculus, not Trichinella
questions.question: Cyclops is intermediate host for the following EXCEPT ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Diphyllobothrium latum does use Cyclops as its first intermediate host, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Diphyllobothrium mansoni, like D. latum, uses Cyclops as an intermediate host, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Correct. Trichinella spiralis is the exception, since it does not use Cyclops, or any other aquatic intermediate host, at all -- man is infected directly by ingesting undercooked meat (classically pork) that already contains encysted infective larvae. Diphyllobothrium latum, Diphyllobothrium mansoni and Dracunculus medinensis, by contrast, all require the tiny freshwater crustacean Cyclops as an obligatory intermediate host, in which their larvae must develop before becoming infective. Man acquires Diphyllobothrium by eating undercooked fish that has itself eaten infected Cyclops, and acquires Dracunculus directly by swallowing infected Cyclops in drinking water.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dracunculus medinensis uses Cyclops as its sole intermediate host, and man is infected by swallowing infected Cyclops in drinking water, so it is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Trichinella spiralis as the exception to Cyclops-borne transmission, since it is food-borne.

questions.title: Onchocerca volvulus is called the blinding worm
questions.question: Onchocerca volvulus is called ?

explanations.A: Correct. Onchocerca volvulus is known as the 'blinding worm' because chronic onchocerciasis is one of the leading infectious causes of blindness worldwide. Microfilariae released by adult worms in subcutaneous nodules migrate through the skin and into the eye, where the resulting inflammatory reaction to dying microfilariae progressively damages the cornea, iris and retina, eventually causing irreversible blindness (river blindness). This ocular damage, rather than the adult worm itself being visible, is what earns Onchocerca its name.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 'Eye worm' is the common name for Loa loa, whose adult worm is sometimes seen migrating visibly across the subconjunctiva, not for Onchocerca volvulus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 'Thread worm' is not the standard eponym for Onchocerca volvulus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 'Guinea worm' is the common name for Dracunculus medinensis, not for Onchocerca volvulus.

questions.learning_objective: Identify 'blinding worm' as the eponym for Onchocerca volvulus, distinguishing it from Loa loa's 'eye worm'.

questions.title: Onchocerca volvulus is transmitted by Simulium
questions.question: Onchocerca volvulus is transninted by ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Culex mosquitoes transmit Wuchereria bancrofti, not Onchocerca volvulus.
explanations.B: Correct. Onchocerca volvulus is transmitted by Simulium, the blackfly, which breeds in fast-flowing rivers and streams. During a blood meal taken near the riverbank, an infected Simulium fly deposits infective third-stage larvae onto the skin, and it is this river-breeding vector, together with the blindness the infection can cause, that gives onchocerciasis its common name, 'river blindness'. No other biting fly or mosquito transmits Onchocerca volvulus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Mansonia mosquitoes transmit Brugia malayi, not Onchocerca volvulus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Chrysops (the mango fly) transmits Loa loa, not Onchocerca volvulus.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Simulium as the vector of Onchocerca volvulus, reversed framing of the same fact as Q146 (reuses its concept).

questions.title: River blindness is due to Onchocerca volvulus
questions.question: River blindness is due to ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Brugia malayi causes lymphatic filariasis (lymphoedema and elephantiasis), not river blindness.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Loa loa causes Calabar swellings and subconjunctival worm migration ('eye worm'), not river blindness.
explanations.C: Correct. River blindness, or onchocerciasis, is caused by Onchocerca volvulus. The disease takes its name from the riverine breeding habitat of its Simulium blackfly vector, and blindness results from the inflammatory reaction to microfilariae dying within ocular tissues after migrating there from subcutaneous nodules harbouring the adult worms. Onchocerciasis remains one of the leading infectious causes of preventable blindness in endemic parts of Africa and Central/South America.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Mansonella ozzardi infection is typically mild or asymptomatic and is not associated with river blindness.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Onchocerca volvulus as the cause of river blindness.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 11, pp.131-132

questions.title: Elephantiasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti
questions.question: Elephantiasis is caused by ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Onchocerca volvulus causes subcutaneous nodules and blindness (river blindness), not elephantiasis.
explanations.B: Correct. Elephantiasis, the gross, disfiguring lymphoedematous swelling classically affecting the lower limbs, scrotum or breasts, is caused by chronic lymphatic filariasis due to Wuchereria bancrofti. The adult worms live coiled within the lymphatics and lymph nodes, and years of chronic lymphatic inflammation, obstruction and secondary bacterial infection eventually produce progressive fibrosis and the thickened, 'elephant-hide' skin that gives the disease its name. Brugia malayi can cause a similar picture, but among the options given, Wuchereria bancrofti is the classic cause.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Loa loa causes Calabar swellings, not the lymphatic obstruction that produces elephantiasis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Mansonella perstans infection is typically mild or asymptomatic and is not a cause of elephantiasis.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Wuchereria bancrofti as the classic cause of elephantiasis.

questions.title: Loa loa is the African eye worm
questions.question: Which of the following parasites is the African eye worm ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Toxocara canis is the dog roundworm responsible for visceral (and ocular) larva migrans in man, not the classic African eye worm.
explanations.B: Correct. Loa loa is known as the African eye worm because the adult worm migrates through subcutaneous and connective tissues across the body, and it can sometimes be seen, and even felt by the patient, moving visibly beneath the conjunctiva of the eye. This striking, directly visible sign is unique among the human filarial worms and is often what first brings the infection to medical attention. Loa loa also causes transient, migratory Calabar swellings elsewhere in the subcutaneous tissue.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Onchocerca volvulus is known as the blinding worm because of the blindness caused by ocular microfilarial damage, not because the adult worm itself is seen migrating across the eye.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Mansonella ozzardi infection is typically mild or asymptomatic and is not known for visible ocular worm migration.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Loa loa as the African eye worm.

questions.title: Creeping eruption is caused by non-human hookworm larvae
questions.question: Creeping eruption is caused by skin penetration of ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The filariform larvae of the human hookworms, Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus, penetrate the skin but then migrate through the bloodstream to the lungs and small intestine rather than remaining trapped in the skin, so they do not typically cause creeping eruption.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Non-human schistosome cercariae cause a different condition, cercarial dermatitis (swimmer's itch), a brief itchy rash at the site of penetration, not the migrating, snake-like track of creeping eruption.
explanations.C: Correct. Creeping eruption (cutaneous larva migrans) results from skin penetration by the filariform larvae of non-human (animal) hookworms, classically Ancylostoma caninum and Ancylostoma braziliense, which normally infect dogs and cats. Because these larvae are adapted to a non-human host, they cannot complete their normal migratory cycle in man and instead wander aimlessly within the epidermis, producing an intensely itchy, serpiginous (snake-like) track that advances slowly over days to weeks. This is distinct from human hookworm species, whose filariform larvae, once they penetrate human skin, do complete the normal migratory route to the lungs and small intestine rather than remaining confined to the skin.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Strongyloides stercoralis larvae can cause a related but distinct migratory skin condition called larva currens, which moves much faster (centimetres per hour) than the slower creeping eruption caused by non-human hookworm larvae.

questions.learning_objective: Identify non-human hookworm larvae as the cause of creeping eruption, reusing lane 10's Ancylostoma caninum CLM concept.

questions.title: Schistosoma is the exception to bare-foot soil infection
questions.question: Man get infected with the following while walking bare footed on the soil EXCEPT ?

explanations.A: Correct. Schistosoma is the exception, since its infective cercarial stage penetrates the skin during contact with contaminated fresh water (such as wading, swimming or washing in an infested canal or lake), not while walking barefoot on dry or moist soil. Ancylostoma duodenale, Strongyloides stercoralis and the non-human hookworm larvae responsible for creeping eruption (cutaneous larva migrans) all instead infect by direct skin penetration of infective larvae present in contaminated soil, which is why bare feet on contaminated ground is the classic risk factor for these three. Wearing shoes is protective against all three soil-transmitted skin-penetrating nematodes but does not protect against Schistosoma, which requires avoiding contact with infested water instead.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ancylostoma duodenale filariform larvae actively penetrate the skin of bare feet in contact with contaminated soil, making it a true example of barefoot soil transmission, not the exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Creeping eruption (cutaneous larva migrans) is caused by non-human hookworm larvae penetrating bare skin in contact with contaminated soil, making it a true example, not the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Strongyloides stercoralis filariform larvae also actively penetrate bare skin in contact with contaminated soil, making it a true example, not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Schistosoma as the exception among bare-foot soil infections, since it is water-transmitted.

questions.title: Elephantiasis is diagnosed by finding microfilaria in blood
questions.question: Elephantiasis is diagnosed by finding in blood ?

explanations.A: Correct. Lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis) due to Wuchereria bancrofti is diagnosed by finding microfilariae circulating in the peripheral blood. Because Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae characteristically show nocturnal periodicity, appearing in greatest numbers in the peripheral blood at night, a blood sample for microscopy is best taken between roughly 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. to maximise the chance of detection. The adult worms themselves remain sequestered within the lymphatics and lymph nodes and are not found circulating in the blood, so it is the released microfilarial offspring, not the adults, that provide the diagnostic blood stage.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Filariform larvae are the skin-penetrating infective stage of soil-transmitted nematodes such as hookworm, not a diagnostic blood stage of lymphatic filariasis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sporozoites are a stage of sporozoan protozoa such as Plasmodium, not of a filarial nematode like Wuchereria bancrofti.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Adult Wuchereria bancrofti worms remain within the lymphatics and are not found circulating in the peripheral blood.

questions.learning_objective: Identify microfilaria in a nocturnal blood film as the diagnostic test for elephantiasis.

questions.title: Chrysops (the mango fly) is the vector of Loa loa
questions.question: Arthropod vector of Loa Loa is ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Mansonia mosquitoes transmit Brugia malayi, not Loa loa.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Black fly (Simulium) transmits Onchocerca volvulus, not Loa loa.
explanations.C: Correct. The arthropod vector of Loa loa is Chrysops, also known as the mango fly or deer fly, a day-biting tabanid fly found in the forested regions of West and Central Africa. Unlike the other human filarial worms, which are transmitted by night-biting mosquitoes or river-breeding Simulium blackflies, Loa loa is transmitted during the day, when Chrysops flies are actively feeding, which is consistent with Loa loa microfilariae showing diurnal (daytime) periodicity in the peripheral blood. An infected Chrysops fly deposits infective larvae onto the skin during a bite, from where they enter the wound.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Female culex mosquitoes transmit Wuchereria bancrofti, not Loa loa.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Chrysops (the mango fly) as the vector of Loa loa.
